chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام:
Regarding a man who bought a house with slaves, goods, cloth, and jewels, he said: “There is no shuf‘ah for anyone in it.”

key_terms.بِرَقِيقٍ: with slaves, as part of the exchange value
key_terms.دَارًا: a house or residence being purchased
key_terms.شُفْعَةٌ: the legal right of pre-emption in a shared property context
key_terms.مَتَاعٍ: goods or personal property used in the transaction

ai.seo_question: Is there a right of shuf‘ah when a house is bought with goods and property rather than cash?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning shuf‘ah in a property sale. It states that when a house is purchased in exchange for items such as slaves, goods, cloth, and jewels, no one has a right of pre-emption in that transaction.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3379 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Abu Abdullah (as):

Regarding a man who bought a house using slaves, goods, fabric, and jewels.
Imam (as) said: "There is no preemption (shufah) for anyone in this case."
